blocks.text: Introduction to Hardy Weinberg Principle

The Hardy Weinberg principle is a fundamental concept in genetics that describes how genetic variation is maintained in a population over time. It states that allele and genotype frequencies in a population will remain constant from generation to generation in the absence of other evolutionary influences.
This principle is based on several assumptions, including a large and randomly mating population, no mutation, no gene flow, and no natural selection.
